notebook: PLAN: Start with a sharp C5/C6+ split to measure cost and separability; then build the most valuable blend/pure-product branches and prune low-value separations. Step 1: test the root column.

note: Switch the root to a C4-/C5+ split at lower pressure, then split the heavy stream at C5/C6 to target the valuable C5 blend.
notebook:
PLAN: Build a high-value blend-first plant: root C4-/C5+, then recover a C5 blend and C6-paraffin blend; add naphthene and light-product branches only where revenue exceeds cost. Step 2: sharpen root C4/C5 cut and test the C5/C6 splitter.
Root at 50/3/3/dp0.1 gave only 1046 mol/s overhead and no products; higher pressure drops in other plants improve the C5 cut. The initial target is ~864 mol/s C4- overhead. Heavy branch should yield ~695 mol/s C5 blend overhead if sharp.

note: Add a C4/C5 splitter for the C5 blend and substantially sharpen the C6-paraffin/naphthene split.
notebook:
PLAN: Build a high-value blend-first plant: root C4-/C5+, recover C5 blend from T and C6-paraffin blend from B; only then consider further branches. Step 2: sharpen both child splitters.
Root 60/3/3/dp0.5 gives 1393 mol/s T containing ~695 C5 and ~628 C4; B is 1907 mol/s C6+. A single C4/C5 column on T should sell its bottoms as C5 blend. B needs a difficult C6-paraffin/MCP cut, so test 80 stages R=B=5. Current root+B cost $389M/yr; C5+C6 blend revenue could exceed $1.1B/yr if both splitters hit 95%.

note: Shift all three cuts heavier with higher boil-up: keep all C5 in the light branch, reject all C4 from the C5 blend, and recover the heavy C6 paraffins in the blend cut.
notebook:
PLAN: Build a high-value blend-first plant: root C4+C5/C6+, recover C5 blend from T and C6-paraffin blend from B; only then consider further branches. Step 2: move both cuts heavier by increasing boil-up so C5 and C6 paraffins are not lost to bottoms.
Root 60/3/3/dp0.5 put ~165 mol/s N-pentane in B. T 60/4/4 left ~230 N-butane in TB, preventing C5 sale. B 80/5/5 made BT only 81% C6 paraffin and lost heavy paraffins to BB. Raising reboil ratio should increase distillate flow: try root B=5, T B=6, B B=7. R128 confirms a third C4/C5 splitter can sell C5 but its six-column backbone is uneconomic; aim for sale with three columns.

note: Focus only on the C5 blend: push residual butane overhead and dimethylbutane into the heavy branch, while deleting the unsold C6 columns.
notebook:
PLAN: Establish a profitable two-column C5-blend plant before adding any C6 recovery. Current step: sharpen root C5/DMB and T C4/C5 cuts, and remove the costly unsold B branch.
Previous three-column plant cost $714M and sold nothing. At root B=5 and T B=6, TB was 72% C5 with ~131 mol/s N-butane and ~165 DMB; raising both boil-up ratios should move butane overhead and DMB to root bottoms. Target TB >=95% C5 (~$527M/yr). Root+T cost about $484M previously, so this can approach breakeven; if purity works, reduce stages/reflux and pressure costs next.

note: Adopt the cheaper root cut and sharpen the C4/C5 column with more stages and reflux but lower boil-up to retain isopentane in the blend.
notebook:
PLAN: Establish a profitable two-column C5-blend plant before adding C6 recovery. Current step: use the cheaper R223 root and sharpen only the C4/C5 splitter.
R223's root gave a nearly ideal 1508 mol/s C5- tops at $202M/yr; its TB was 82% C5 with 13% n-butane and 3% DMB. My prior high boil-up (8) wrongly drove isopentane overhead. Increase T to 100 stages and reflux 8, reduce boil-up to 3, targeting >95% C5 while retaining isopentane. Potential blend revenue is about $609M/yr versus roughly $400M column cost. If purity works, then reduce stages/reflux and root pressure cost.

note: Copy the profitable C6-blend configuration and strengthen its C4/C5 splitter enough to exceed the 95% C5-blend specification.
notebook:
PLAN: Start from R268's proven saleable C6-paraffin branch, then make its C5 blend saleable and finally reduce cost. Current step: strengthen the C4/C5 splitter while preserving the root and C6 column.
R268 earns 0.885 with root 70/3/4/.45 and B 110/6/7/.15; BT is a saleable C6-paraffin blend worth $1119M/yr. Its TB is only 88% C5, with 9% n-butane and 3% DMB. My own tests show boil-up 3 is far too low (C5 goes overhead), while R223 at 5 and R268 at 7 progressively improve C5 bottoms purity. Copy R268 and raise T to 150 stages, reflux 10, boil-up 9 to remove butane and DMB. After crossing 95%, optimize the expensive T column downward and consider C4 recovery only if economics justify it.

note: Copy the best C5/C6 plant and increase the C5 polisher's separation and boil-up to recover the large C5 loss in its overhead.
notebook:
PLAN: Use the proven C6 backbone, then maximize C5-blend recovery with a dedicated C4/C5 polisher; afterward reduce column costs. Current step: strengthen R314's polisher to recover the one-third of C5 currently lost overhead.
Copy R314 (reward 1.716): root 70/3/4/.45, T 110/6/7/0, B 110/6/7/.15. Its BT sells for $1119M/yr and TBB C5 blend for $417M/yr. TB=70/4/3/.1 loses about 228 mol/s C5 to TBT; higher boil-up should retain it in TBB while C4 goes overhead. DMB is only ~4% of TBB, so stronger splitting may also improve purity. Test TB=100/6/6/.1, then tune downward for cost or upward if recovery/purity remains limiting.

note: Combine the best C5 recovery configuration with the proven C4-blend recovery column on TT.
notebook:
PLAN: Start from R364's best four-column C5/C6 plant, monetize the light TT stream as a C4 blend, then optimize the added column and reduce expensive backbone duties. Current step: add the proven TT C3/C4 splitter.
R364 (2.113) uses root 70/3/4/.45, T 110/6/7/0, B 110/6/7/.15, TB 70/6/1.2/.1. Its low-boilup TB retains 666 mol/s C5 blend worth $567M/yr at only $28.4M cost. R361 proved TT 70/4/4/0 yields a $149.3M C4 blend for $50.9M cost, although its C3 tops remain unsold due ethane/isobutane. Combining these should add about 0.22 reward. Next test lower TT stages/duties while retaining 95% C4, then investigate backbone cost reductions.

note: Reduce both large splitters from 110/6/7 to 100/5/6 to seek substantial energy and size savings without sharply moving the established cuts.
notebook:
PLAN: Preserve the profitable C4/C5/C6 products while reducing the very expensive backbone duties, then optimize TT and consider heavy-product recovery. Current step: test moderate T/B stage and duty reductions.
Best is 2.337: root 70/3/4/.45; T,B 110/6/7; TB 70/6/1.2/.1; TT 70/4/4. Revenue 1835, costs 810. BT C6 blend $1119M, TBB C5 $567M, TTB C4 $149M. TBT and BB are unsold. TB's low boil-up is crucial for C5 recovery and cheap. Backbone columns cost $731M combined, so modest duty reductions are the clearest next gain. Test T and B at 100/5/6 while retaining their pressure drops; inspect purity and flow shifts before more aggressive cuts.

note: Combine the independently proven cheaper light splitter with the current C6 splitter to reduce cost without changing either product cut.
notebook:
PLAN: Preserve the profitable C4/C5/C6 products while reducing the very expensive backbone duties, then optimize TT and consider heavy-product recovery. Current step: combine the proven cheaper T splitter with my cheaper B splitter.
Best is 2.466: root 70/3/4/.45; T,B 100/5/6; TB 70/6/1.2/.1; TT 70/4/4. Revenue 1826, costs 745. Agent 32 shows T=70/4/5 works with the original B, saving about $26.5M/yr versus my T while preserving all products. Combine it with B=100/5/6 for an expected reward near 2.53. Then test root reductions cautiously: root costs $268M/yr, but its cut must keep C5 out of B and DMB out of T. B=70/4/5 fails C6 purity, so do not reduce B that far.

note: Reduce the root's stages and duties to seek major savings while monitoring the established C5/C6 boundary.
notebook:
PLAN: Preserve the profitable C4/C5/C6 products while reducing the very expensive backbone duties, then optimize TT and consider heavy-product recovery. Current step: test a cheaper root column.
Best is 2.529: root 70/3/4/.45; B=100/5/6/.15; T=70/4/5/0; TB=70/6/1.2/.1; TT=70/4/4. Revenue 1827, cost 718. Root costs $268M/yr and is the largest target. Test 60/2.5/3.5, checking especially that C5 stays out of B and DMB stays out of T. B=70/4/5 is known to fail C6 purity. TTT is only 81% C3 and TBT is a small waste stream, so backbone savings remain preferable.

note: Restore the best plant and moderately reduce the light C4/C5 splitter, which has purity margin in both downstream products.
notebook:
PLAN: Preserve the profitable C4/C5/C6 products while reducing the very expensive backbone duties, then optimize TT and consider heavy-product recovery. Current step: test a cheaper T splitter after restoring the best design.
Best is 2.529: root 70/3/4/.45; B=100/5/6/.15; T=70/4/5/0; TB=70/6/1.2/.1; TT=70/4/4. Revenue 1827, cost 718. Root 60/2.5/3.5 failed C6 purity and lost C5 revenue. B=90/4.5/5.5 and 100/5/8 also fail C6 purity, so retain B=100/5/6. Test T=60/3.5/4.5; C5 currently has modest purity margin and C4 blend is essentially uncontaminated. TTT only 81% C3 and TBT small, so backbone savings remain preferable.

note: Recover both valuable fractions of the small TBT stream with an easy N-butane/C5 split; its combined product value should comfortably cover a small column.
notebook:
PLAN: Preserve the profitable C4/C5/C6 products, recover valuable small side streams where column cost is modest, then optimize the backbone. Current step: split TBT into pure N-butane and a C5 blend.
Best is 2.561: root 70/3/4/.45; B=100/5/6/.15; T=60/3.5/4.5/0; TB=70/6/1.2/.1; TT=70/4/4. Revenue 1828, cost 705. TBT contains about 69 mol/s N-butane and 54 mol/s C5, potentially $83M/yr if both outlets meet specs; an easy small splitter should cost much less. Root/B reductions have repeatedly failed C6 purity, so avoid weakening B. Later consider TTT ethane removal and cheaper TT settings.

note: Combine the independently proven low-cost TT column with higher TBT boil-up, aiming to push the residual butane overhead and qualify its C5-rich bottoms.
notebook:
PLAN: Preserve the profitable C4/C5/C6 products, recover valuable small side streams where column cost is modest, then optimize the backbone. Current step: combine the proven cheap TT with a stronger TBT boil-up to eliminate residual butane from its C5 bottoms.
Best reward 2.600: revenue 1852.9, cost 712.6. R652 proves TT=40/2.5/3 saves about $13M/yr with negligible product loss. TBT currently gives 56 mol/s pure butane and 67 mol/s bottoms containing 54 C5 plus 13 butane; increasing boil-up from 3 to 4.5 should push enough butane overhead for the 95% C5 blend, adding about $48M/yr if successful. Do not weaken B or T: prior reductions destroyed the valuable C6 blend. Remaining ideas: optimize TBT settings, then TTT ethane rejection if economical.

note: Test compact ethane rejection followed by C3/C4 splitting on the unsold TTT stream; the available C3 and C4 value may cover two small columns.
notebook:
PLAN: Preserve the profitable C4/C5/C6 products, recover valuable small side streams where column cost is modest, then optimize the backbone. Current step: test a compact two-column ethane/C3/C4 recovery on TTT; if uneconomic, revert and use remaining solves on modest backbone cost reductions.
Best reward 2.742: revenue 1903.1, cost 700.8. TBT=50/3/4.5 now sells both premium butane and its C5 bottoms. TTT contains about 286 mol/s C3 worth roughly $60-70M/yr as a blend, plus 41 mol/s C4, but also 34 ethane. A deethanizer followed by C3/C4 splitting may recover these for less than their value. Do not weaken B or T: prior reductions destroyed the valuable C6 blend. TT=40/2.5/3 is proven cheaper. If TTT recovery fails, revert and test root 60 stages or TBT trimming.

note: Sharpen the small C3/C4 splitter to recover the large C3 loss in its bottoms and potentially qualify that bottoms as a C4 blend.
notebook:
PLAN: Preserve the profitable C4/C5/C6 products, recover valuable small side streams where column cost is modest, then optimize the backbone. Current step: sharpen TTTB to recover nearly all C3 overhead and qualify its C4-rich bottoms; if uneconomic, revert and trim backbone cost.
Best reward 2.787. The two small TTT columns add net value. TTTBT sells 138 mol/s pure C3 for $35.3M/yr, but TTTBB still contains about 111 mol/s C3 and 41 C4. A sharper 60-stage, reflux 4, boil-up 4.5 split could sell about $65M/yr C3 plus a small C4 blend, likely worth its modest cost. Do not weaken B or T: prior reductions destroyed the valuable C6 blend. TT=40/2.5/3 and TBT=50/3/4.5 are proven. Root/B/T are expensive and sensitive.

note: Adopt R797's cheaper, higher-recovery C3/C4 splitter, which gives the best valid island reward while preserving all proven backbone products.
notebook:
PLAN: Adopt the island's best proven plant, then use remaining solves only on low-risk leaf-column cost or recovery improvements. Current step: copy R797 (40-stage TTTB at reflux 2.5 and boil-up 4.5), which improves C3 recovery and lowers cost.
Best team/own target reward 2.803. R797 recovers 168 mol/s C3 overhead versus 141 in my last design and cuts TTTB cost to $5.0M/yr. Backbone products are valuable and sensitive: BT is only about 95% C6 blend, so avoid weakening B without a quick revert. TT, TB and TBT settings are proven. Remaining ideas: test TTTB boil-up 5.5 for extra C3 recovery; optionally test B pressure drop 0.25 for energy savings, then revert if BT purity or economics worsen.

note: Test two independent upside moves from R844: additional C3 recovery in the tiny splitter and lower-pressure operation of the costly heavy splitter.
notebook:
PLAN: Start from the island-best R844 (TTTB boil-up 6), then use the remaining budget on one stronger C3-recovery test and one independent heavy-column energy test; revert immediately if either hurts.
R844 scores 2.814: boil-up 6 lifts C3 revenue to $48.2M/yr for only $0.4M/yr extra cost. C3 overhead remains 100% blend while 102 mol/s bottoms still contain about 59 mol/s C3, so boil-up 8 may add value. B costs $238.8M/yr and is a leaf; raising its pressure drop from 0.15 to 0.25 may reduce heating/cooling cost without altering the other seven columns. BT is near the 95% C6-blend boundary, so reject any purity loss. If this combined test fails, restore R844 and test only TTTB at 8.

note: Extend both independently profitable trends: slightly lower B operating pressure for additional C6 recovery, and higher small-column boil-up for further C3 recovery. Revert if C6 blend purity is lost.
notebook:
PLAN: With seven solves left, extend the two profitable local trends (B pressure drop and TTTB boil-up), then retain the best valid point and avoid purity-threatening structural changes.
Current 2.841 uses B dp .25 and TTTB boil-up 8. Versus dp .15, B dp .25 adds $14.3M C6 revenue for $7.2M cost, so test .30; BT is near 95% paraffin purity, making this the main risk. C3 recovery rises steadily from boil-up 6 through 8, with overhead still qualified, so test 10. B at 95 stages destroyed blend purity and must not be reduced. Remaining unsold streams are too small or difficult to justify new columns.

note: Build on R934's island-best plant and extend both independent profitable trends: higher B pressure for C6 recovery and boil-up 10 for additional C3 recovery.
notebook:
PLAN: With five solves left, adopt the island-best 2.857 point, extend the still-profitable heavy-column pressure and C3 boil-up trends, then retain the best valid design.
R934 (B dp .35, TTTB boil-up 9) scores 2.857. My boil-up 10 remains profitable at B dp .30. B pressure increases from .15 to .35 have steadily added C6 revenue faster than cost; test .45 with boil-up 10. BT remains qualified at 95% paraffin purity, so monitor that threshold. B stages below 100 previously destroyed blend purity; do not repeat. Remaining unsold streams are too small or difficult to justify added columns.

note: Restore the island-best heavy-column setting and extend the cheap C3 recovery trend to boil-up 12, leaving the delicate C6 blend cut unchanged.
notebook:
PLAN: Restore R976 (2.860), use the remaining solves on the low-risk C3 recovery trend, and stop if it saturates or purity fails.
R976 is the safe optimum: B dp .35 keeps BT just above the C6-blend threshold; .40 and .45 destroy about $1136M/yr of sales, so never increase it further. TTTB boil-up 9->10 added 6 mol/s C3 product for only $0.1M/yr cost. Test 12 now; if the trend continues, one higher setting may recover more of the roughly 249 mol/s C3 entering that column. Other unsold streams are too small or difficult to justify new columns.

note: Use the final available column solve on boil-up 13; 12 was still marginally profitable, while 15 is clearly too costly, so this brackets the economic limit.
notebook:
PLAN: Finish the low-risk C3 recovery sweep with one final boil-up increment, then stop; retain 2.865 if the gain no longer covers energy cost.
Boil-up 9->10->11->12 steadily recovered saleable C3, but R1016 shows 15 is uneconomic because cost rises sharply. Test 13 only. B dp .35 is essential: .40 destroys the entire $1136M/yr C6 blend, and extra reflux at .36 also loses value. No other small unsold stream justifies another column.
